content.readme:
# DeepInfer

DeepInfer is the high-performance inference framework that powers DeepSeek's large-scale production services. This open-source release provides offline inference with the core features needed for serving at scale.

Supported models:

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

Supported features:

- Optimized kernels, model and sampler runtime
- Parallelism: Attention DP / balanced CP, MoE EP + EPLB
- DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification
- SWA bounded replay
- Asynchronous scheduling (zero-overhead batch scheduler)
- Batch-invariant inference
- Deterministic sampling
- Structured outputs

<details>
<summary>Feature details and configuration</summary>

- **Optimized kernels:** [FlashMLA](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/FlashMLA), [DeepGEMM](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM), [DeepEP](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP), [TileKernels](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/TileKernels), [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect), and custom [TileLang kernels](deepinfer/model_executor/layers/tilelang_ops).
- **DSpark and confidence-scheduled verification:** accelerate decoding with draft tokens and use confidence estimates to schedule verification. Set `DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=1`; `DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE` controls the maximum draft length (default: 5).
- **Decoder SWA bounded replay:** reduce decoder prefill work by replaying only a bounded suffix. Set `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_TRUNCATION_MODE=compact` and `DEEPINFER_YOCO_PREFILL_KEEP_TOKENS=140` for the default V4.1 settings; the retained suffix must cover the SWA window plus the maximum backtracking length.
- **Asynchronous scheduling:** overlap CPU batch scheduling with device execution. Enabled by default.
- **Batch-invariant inference:** keep model results identical across different batch compositions. Enable with `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` (NVIDIA only).
- **Deterministic sampling:** produce identical outputs for identical input tokens and sampling parameters. Set `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0` and pass a fixed `seq_seed` to `SamplingParams` (NVIDIA only).
- **Structured outputs:** constrain generation to a regex, JSON schema, or EBNF grammar. Pass `so_args={"schema_type": ..., "schema": ...}` to `SamplingParams`; see [examples](examples/_structured_output.py).

</details>

Supported hardware:

- NVIDIA SM100 GPUs
- Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs

Required for a complete inference service (not included in this release):

- A KV cache system
- VE/Prefill/Decode disaggregation (most required engine functionality is already implemented)
- Load balancing across data-parallel replicas for both prefill and decode

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Linux
- GCC >= 13.0
- Python 3.12
- CUDA 13 (NVIDIA only)
- CANN 9.2 (Ascend only)

### Build from source

Before building DeepInfer, please create and activate an empty Python 3.12 environment.

``` bash
# Use `ascend` instead for the Ascend platform
# Keep it exported in the environment where you run DeepInfer
export DEEPINFER_ACCELERATOR=nvidia
./build.sh
```

### Offline inference

The default checkpoint, [`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), is
downloaded into the Hugging Face cache on the first run; set `DEEPINFER_HF_MODEL_DIR=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` to
run from a local copy instead.

``` bash
python examples/offline_inference.py
```

See [examples](examples/README.md) for details.

## Performance benchmarks

| Prefill | Decode |
| :---: | :---: |
| [![Prefill: non-cached input throughput vs. latency](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png)](doc/images/prefill_pareto.png) | [![Decode: output throughput vs. per-user speed](doc/images/decode_pareto.png)](doc/images/decode_pareto.png) |

Measured on 4 SM100 GPUs for prefill and 64 for decode — each within one scale-up domain. To reproduce the benchmarks, see [run_sweep.sh](examples/sweep/run_sweep.sh).

## Evaluation benchmarks

See [eval/README.md](eval/README.md).

## License

DeepInfer is released under the Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

## Acknowledgments

DeepInfer was originally built primarily on [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), with additional inspiration from [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) and [TensorRT-LLM](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM). We thank their developers.

## Citation

```bibtex
@misc{deepinfer2026,
  title = {DeepInfer: High-performance, large-scale inference framework for DeepSeek models},
  author = {DeepSeek-AI},
  year = {2026},
  publisher = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepInfer}},
}
```

Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World

A **harness** is the system around a model that enables it to act as an agent: prompts, tools, memory, skills, orchestration, and more. **Harnessing** is the process of optimizing that system. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework for **recursive agent harnessing** in an open world, where agents encounter tasks unseen during harness design. It connects two levels of recursion while keeping model weights fixed: * **Task-level recursion** refines the execution harness for the current task through a contrastive **Propose–Probe–Compose** step: propose edits, probe their effects on the same task, and compose a refined harness from behavioral contrasts between executions, without ground-truth feedback. * **Harnessing-level recursion** updates a persistent *improvement harness* with adopted harnesses and evidence-supported lessons from each task to guide future refinement.

Across three professional benchmarks and four model–harness configurations, a single Harness² step improves GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash over their base harnesses, with gains of up to 11.5 points on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5 points on JobBench, and 11.8 percentage points on LAB's partial pass rate. Increasing the task-level recursion budget brings further gains. The release supports **parallel and sequential recursion**, **OpenCode and Codex executors**, and **JobBench, LAB, and WorkBuddy-Bench**. ## Video overview https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b10548-b14b-4c8f-9aa5-a93662df4d56 ## Contents - [Video overview](#video-overview) - [Harness components](#harness-components) - [Install](#install) - [Run a benchmark](#run-a-benchmark) - [Experiments](#experiments) - [Web access](#web-access) - [Results and resume](#results-and-resume) - [Citation](#citation) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) - [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) ## Harness components Harness² exposes eight editable components around the model: **system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, and plugins**. They control context construction, the tool interface, delegation, and behavior inside the tool loop.

## Install Use **Linux, Python 3.12, and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)**. From the repository root: ```bash uv venv --python 3.12 .venv source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e '.[render]' harness2-demo --output runs/demo --k 2 ``` The local demo runs both recursion modes with deterministic editors and real Python executions. It requires no model credentials. For model-backed benchmarks, install **Node.js 20+, the Google Cloud CLI**, and the [benchmark dependencies](docs/SETUP.md#requirements). # nxnative Play your own Nintendo Switch games natively on iPhone and iPad. Bring your game (its NSP files) and your `prod.keys`; one script turns them into an IPA that you sideload. It is not an emulator: the game's own code runs directly on the Apple chip, with Switch graphics rebuilt on Metal. Nothing from any game is in this repository, and the project is not affiliated with Nintendo or any game publisher. ## How to play ### With a Mac app Community projects build on nxnative with Mac apps that turn your games into apps for your iPhone, iPad or Mac, with no command line, and keep them in a library. They are separate projects: questions and bugs about them go to their own pages. - [NX2Apple](https://github.com/LNPANDY/NX2Apple) - [NX Play](https://github.com/varyform/nx-native-wrapper) - [NxNative Launcher](https://github.com/rennan101/nxnative_Launcher) - [LumaNX](https://github.com/Xc1Ym/LumaNX) ### Build from the command line You need a Mac with macOS 26.6 or later, [Xcode](https://developer.apple.com/download/all/?q=Xcode%2027.2) 27.2, [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) and Python 3.12 or newer (an arm64 one, not an Intel Homebrew's). An iPhone build also needs Xcode's iOS platform (Xcode → Settings → Components). The shaders are built with Xcode 27.2's Metal compiler. Select it before step 1: `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app`. With several Xcode versions installed, name this one `Xcode-27.2.app` and select it with `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode-27.2.app`. **1. Install the tools** (only once), in Terminal: ``` xcodebuild -downloadComponent MetalToolchain git clone https://github.com/seedds/nxnative.git && cd nxnative brew install xcodegen zstd glslang brew install --cask dotnet-sdk python3 -m pip install lz4 "capstone>=5,<6" fonttools nsz zbic "backports.zstd; python_version < '3.14'" ``` **2. Put your game in a folder**: the game, plus its update and DLC if you have them (`.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nsz` or `.xcz`): ``` ~/Games/MarioWonder/ Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514000][v0].nsp Super Mario Bros. Wonder [010015100B514800][v327680].nsp ``` **3. Build**, with your game folder and your `prod.keys`: ``` python3 scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py ~/Games/MarioWonder -k ~/keys/prod.keys ``` The IPA appears in the game's folder. The first build takes 30–60 minutes and needs free disk space of about twice the game's size plus 10 GB; building again is much faster. To play on the Mac instead, add `--platform mac-app`: you get a Mac app of the game to open from Finder. All options: [The packing script in detail](docs/development.md#the-packing-script-in-detail). ### Install Install the IPA on your iPhone or iPad with a sideloading tool such as AltStore, Sideloadly or LiveContainer. If your tool offers **Increased Memory Limit**, turn it on: the bigger games need it. Game too big to install? Build again with `--romfs separate`, and run the command the script prints once to copy the game files to your phone ([Quick reinstalls](docs/development.md#quick-reinstalls)). Controls, saves and settings: [Playing](docs/playing.md). ## Games Games tested on Mac or iPhone. See the [per-game notes](dm/games/README.md#games) for tested platforms, progress and known issues: Needs iOS / iPadOS 26 or later on an iPhone 15 Pro or newer (A17 Pro chip or later) or an iPad with an M1 chip or later: the games' textures are BC-compressed, and older iPhones can't read that format. Other games aren't supported yet. For them the script writes a survey and still tries its best to pack an IPA, guessing the game's settings; such an IPA may not start. Under a game, "60 fps with 1.2.0" means it runs at 60 fps (30 on the Switch) with that update.

content.readme:
# The Replica skill

Eleven Claude skills that clone any app. Free, MIT, no signup, no API key,
nothing to connect.

One reverse-engineers the app you want to clone. One rebuilds it. One tests it
for bugs. And one is the Entrepreneur: it reads what the app's users hate and
fixes it in yours, so you have an app you can sell.

In between, the others plan the stack and the database, rebuild the design
system, wire up auth and payments, score your clone against the original, give
it a name and a brand of its own, write the landing page and the store
listing, and put it live on your domain.

**It rebuilds what an app does, never what it owns.** Features and flows,
clean-room style. Not its code, its logo, its copy or its content. The
fine print is at the bottom, and the skills enforce it.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/replica-skill
/plugin install replica-skill@replica-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/replica-skill:replica-recon` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/replica-recon`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill.git
cp -r replica-skill/replica-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the
method works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install.

## The eleven

| command | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/replica-recon` | Reverse-engineers any app: screens, flows, components, data model. From public pages, screenshots, store listings and your own account. |
| `/replica-architect` | Plans the stack, database schema and API for your clone. |
| `/replica-design` | Rebuilds the design system: colours, type, spacing, components. As tokens, with your own assets. |
| `/replica-build` | Rebuilds the app screen by screen from the recon map. |
| `/replica-backend` | Auth, database, payments and integrations. |
| `/replica-test` | Clicks through every flow and tests it for bugs. |
| `/replica-diff` | Compares your clone against the original. A parity score and what is missing. |
| `/replica-entrepreneur` | Reads what the app's users hate in real reviews and turns it into fixes and a positioning angle. |
| `/replica-brand` | Names and rebrands your version so it is yours. |
| `/replica-launch` | Landing page, pricing and App Store listing. |
| `/replica-deploy` | Ships it live on your own domain. |

## How to use it

Run them in order. Each one reads what the last one wrote, in a `replica/`
folder in your project.

```
recon -> architect -> design -> build -> backend -> test -> diff -> entrepreneur -> brand -> launch -> deploy
```

An example: cloning a scheduling app, the kind where you share a link and
people book a time with you.

1. **`/replica-recon`** with the app's URL. It reads the help center, the
   pricing page, the store listing and public walkthroughs, and you click
   through your own account with it. Out comes `replica/recon.md`: 18
   screens, 7 flows (guest books a meeting, host sets availability, guest
   reschedules...), the components, an inferred data model (users, event
   types, availability, bookings) and `features.csv`. The partner
   marketplace is marked out of scope: that is their network, not a feature.
2. **`/replica-architect`** picks Next.js, Postgres, Stripe and Resend, writes
   the schema (with a constraint so two guests can never book the same slot)
   and orders the build: the booking flow end to end first.
3. **`/replica-design`** measures the screenshots into tokens: colour roles,
   type scale, 8px spacing, the date picker and slot button specs. Open
   icons, an open font, your own words.
4. **`/replica-build`** builds the shell, then the booking flow, then every
   screen with all its states, ticking off `features.csv` as it goes.
5. **`/replica-backend`** adds sign up, Google Calendar through Google's own
   API with your keys, Stripe for paid bookings, reminder emails.
6. **`/replica-test`** writes a test plan from the 7 flows, Playwright specs
   for the happy paths and edge cases (time zones, a slot taken mid-booking,
   double submit), and logs bugs by severity until no S1 or S2 is open.
7. **`/replica-diff`** scores it. Features 86, all must-haves done, booking
   page layout 91. Missing: round-robin for teams, the website embed.
8. **`/replica-entrepreneur`** reads 140 real reviews across the App Store,
   G2, Capterra and Reddit. Top complaints: per-seat price jumps, no text
   reminders, guests confused by time zones. Each with counts and linked
   quotes. Fix plan: flat pricing, SMS reminders, a time zone confirm step.
   Angle: booking links for small teams that hate per-seat pricing.

# iPhone Use

**中文** · [English](README.en.md)

![iPhone Use 在 Codex 中操作真实 iPhone 并实时展示手机屏幕](assets/iphone-use-demo.png)

让 Codex、WorkBuddy 或豆包工作通过 USB 操作你的真实 iPhone。用自然语言描述任务，助手就能打开 App、读取页面、点击、滚动、输入文字、整理列表，并在侧边栏展示手机屏幕。

iPhone Use 使用 [WebDriverAgent](https://github.com/appium/WebDriverAgent)（WDA）与 iPhone 通信，包含本地 MCP 服务、安装与使用技能，以及实时屏幕 widget。它优先复用现有连接与构建；控件定位失败时，指导模型查看截图并尝试坐标点击。

插件默认向独立的 PostHog 项目及 GA4 属性发送匿名使用统计，包括实际使用开始、工具调用、连接状态、耗时、错误类别，以及显式启动的 App 标识和公开目录名称（含 batch 中已完成的启动）。使用随机安装标识，不上传手机画面、输入内容、设备标识或已安装 App 清单。设置 `IPHONE_USE_ANALYTICS=0` 或 `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` 并重启 MCP 服务可关闭。详见 [埋点与分析说明](ANALYTICS.md)。

**使用前，需要先在你自己的 iPhone 上安装、签名并启动 WDA Runner。** WDA 是运行在手机上的执行服务；下面的提示词和 setup 流程可以让所用宿主的助手协助完成首次安装，已有健康的 WDA 可直接复用。

## 最近更新

2026-10-09 至 2026-10-13，完整记录见 [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md)。

- **预览直接操作**：支持点击画面、鼠标拖动和触控板双指滚动。
- **微信点击优化**：已知导航目标直接看图点击，通讯录和会话列表按需轻量读取。
- **AirDrop 文件传输**：使用技能新增传输指引，将手机图片、视频和文档传回 Mac。
- **页面读取优化**：精简控件树，默认最多返回 200 个节点，支持按需限制快照。
- **连接恢复改进**：完善超时与断线指引，自动恢复临时快照设置。
- **长文本续传保护**：续传绑定原输入框，切换 App 或焦点后停止，避免误写。

## 用一段提示词让 Codex 安装

将下面这段话复制到本机 Codex：

```text
请帮我安装和配置 iPhone Use：
https://github.com/zhongerxin/iPhone-use

先读取仓库 README 和安装脚本，检查本机 Codex CLI、Python、Node.js、npm、
完整 Xcode，以及通过 USB 连接的 iPhone。把项目放到合适的本机目录，
运行 sh scripts/install.sh 安装插件。

如果当前聊天还没有加载新工具，明确告诉我重连或新开聊天后继续。
工具可用后读取 iphone-use-setup 技能，检查现有配置，优先复用已有 WDA。
首次配置时发现我的设备，使用我自己的 Apple 开发团队和可签名 bundle ID，
获取固定版本 WDA、配置签名、构建并启动，直到 pua_ready 返回 ready=true，
然后打开手机屏幕。不要照搬作者的设备标识或签名信息。

缺少依赖时说明具体缺项并帮助安装。Apple 账号登录、设备信任、开发者模式
或解锁需要我操作时，告诉我明确步骤，等我完成再继续。
```

安装插件后，当前聊天可能需要重新连接才能加载工具，流程可在重连后继续。Apple 账号登录、设备信任、开发者模式及手机解锁仍需本人在系统界面完成。

仓库目前为私有，需要有 GitHub 访问权限，或者使用已取得的源代码包。

## 在 WorkBuddy 和豆包工作中安装

两者都支持通过 USB 操作真实 iPhone，并在侧边栏显示实时画面；共用本机的设备配置、WDA 构建和操作锁，已配置过的手机优先复用。依赖仍是 macOS、完整 Xcode、Python、Node.js / npm 和 USB iPhone，安装这两个适配版无需 Codex CLI。适配版默认关闭匿名使用统计。

| 宿主 | 在源码目录运行 | 安装后的接入 |

content.readme:
# The Day Trader skill

11 Claude skills for day trading: scan thousands of charts, track breaking news, time every entry and exit, and replay every outcome before you risk a dollar.

Free, MIT, no signup, no API key. The tools are plain Python that read free
public data: Yahoo Finance charts, Nasdaq Trader's symbol lists, SEC EDGAR
and the House Clerk.

One scans thousands of charts for setups. Another tracks breaking news on
every stock you watch. One watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment
to get in, and another sets your stop and your target before you do. And the
craziest one is the Time Machine: before you risk a dollar, it replays the
rest of the session 10,000 times from the stock's own recent bars, plus every
past day the same setup fired, and tells you the honest odds.

And no trade goes through until you say yes. Nothing in this pack can place
an order on its own. Paper trading is the default.

> **Looking for the original Trader skill?** Copy an investor's 13F, the
> stock screener, tax lots and rebalancing live in
> [github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/trader-skill).
> This repo is its day-trading sequel: the Trader skill v2.

## Install

Paste this into Claude:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill
/plugin install day-trader-skill@day-trader-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/day-trader-skill:trader-scanner` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/trader-scanner`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill.git
cp -r day-trader-skill/trader-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the
top of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the Python tools, but the method
works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install. The SEC tools
(news filings, the analyst) ask you to identify yourself: put your name and
email in `trader/config.json` (`"sec_user_agent": "Your Name you@example.com"`)
or in the `SEC_USER_AGENT` environment variable.

## The eleven

| command | job | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/trader-scanner` | Chart Scanner | Scans thousands of charts for setups: opening-range breakouts, flags, oversold bounces. |
| `/trader-news` | News Monitor | Tracks breaking news on every stock you watch and flags what moves it. |
| `/trader-entry` | Entry Timer | Watches a setup bar by bar and tells you the moment to get in. |
| `/trader-exit` | Exit Planner | Sets your stop and your target before you enter, so you know when to get out. |
| `/trader-timemachine` | Time Machine | Replays every possible outcome of a trade before you risk a dollar: 10,000 simulated sessions plus every past time the setup fired. |
| `/trader-risk` | Risk Manager | Checks every trade against your limits and stops anything over them. |
| `/trader-budget` | Budget Manager | Sizes every position to your budget and your max loss per trade. |
| `/trader-broker` | Order Executor | Sends approved orders to your broker, paper trading by default, never without your yes. |
| `/trader-alerts` | Price Alerts | Rings when a price, a stop or the opening bell hits. |
| `/trader-analyst` | Earnings Analyst | Reads earnings reports and sums up what changed. |
| `/trader-pelosi` | Pelosi Tracker | Reads Congress's stock-trade disclosures the minute they are filed. |

## How to use it

Everything lands in a `trader/` folder in your project, and each skill reads
what the last one wrote:

```
scanner -> news -> entry -> exit -> timemachine -> budget -> risk -> broker   (one trade)
alerts: stop, target, flat by the close                                       (while it is open)
news / analyst / pelosi                                                        (on a schedule)
```

An example, the trade in the reel: Tesla, Monday October 19 2026, real data.

1. **`/trader-scanner`** at 10:15 AM ET: of the 231 charts in the reel's
   scan, 42 had closed above their 15-minute opening range. TSLA is one: range 354.47 to 362.18,
   the 10:10 candle closed at 364.18, 0.55 % over the top.
2. **`/trader-news`**: the morning's TSLA headlines, in New York time
   ("Tesla-SpaceX Merger Mania Strikes Wall Street Ahead of Earnings", 8:04,
   tagged earnings and deal). Tesla reports this week: a day trade is out
   before the close, so it is not exposed to the report.
3. **`/trader-entry`** watched TSLA bar by bar. At 10:12 it said waiting (the
   10:10 bar was still forming). At 10:15 it said triggered: the first
   5-minute close above the range, 364.18.
4. **`/trader-exit`** set the plan before the entry: stop at the range's
   midpoint, 358.32, so 5.86 a share at risk; target one times that risk,
   370.04; flat by 3:55 PM either way.

# Zero Breach Toolkit

A free, open-source check for traces of known mercenary spyware (Pegasus, Predator,
Graphite, Candiru and others) on computers, Android phones and iPhone backups.

- **Read-only.** It does not modify source evidence or system settings. It writes only
  temporary database snapshots and the reports you ask for.
- **No network requests during a scan.** It never looks up spyware addresses and has no
  upload feature. Python network calls are blocked and redirected paths are refused. This
  is not an operating-system network sandbox; see [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).
- **States its limits.** Every report says what was found, how strong the evidence is, and
  what could not be checked. A clean result is never presented as proof that you are safe.

Made by archivegenocide. Built on [Zero Breach](https://github.com/interplains/zero-breach).

> **If you think you are being targeted right now, get expert help first.** You do not
> need to run this tool before asking. Journalists, activists, human-rights defenders and
> civil society can contact the
> [Access Now Digital Security Helpline](https://www.accessnow.org/help/) (free, 24/7,
> many languages) or [Amnesty International's Security Lab](https://securitylab.amnesty.org/get-help/).

---

## Step-by-step guide (no technical experience needed)

You do not need a GitHub account or any technical knowledge. You need a Windows or Mac
computer and about 20 minutes. Phones are checked by connecting them to the computer.

**What do you want to check?**
[This Windows computer](#windows) ·
[This Mac](#mac) ·
[An Android phone](#android-phone) ·
[An iPhone](#iphone)

### Windows

**Set up (only the first time)**

1. Go to [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/) and click the yellow
   **Download Python** button. Open the downloaded file.
2. On the first screen of the installer, **tick "Add python.exe to PATH"** at the bottom,
   then click **Install Now**. Wait until it says "Setup was successful".
3. On this page, click the green **Code** button near the top, then **Download ZIP**.
4. Open your **Downloads** folder, right-click **Zero-Breach-Toolkit-main.zip** and choose
   **Extract All**, then **Extract**.

**Run the check**

5. Close your web browsers and chat apps (Chrome, Edge, WhatsApp, Signal…).
6. Open the **Zero-Breach-Toolkit-main** folder (if there is another folder with the same name
   inside, open that one too), then the **scan** folder, and double-click **run-scan.cmd**.
   If Windows shows a warning, click **Run** (or **More info**, then **Run anyway**).
7. A menu appears. Type the number next to **Update the indicator lists** and press Enter,
   then type `y` and press Enter. When it finishes, press Enter.
8. Press Enter again to start **This computer - standard check**. It takes about 15 minutes.
9. Read the result at the end (see [What the result means](#what-the-result-means)). A copy
   is saved in the **findings** folder inside Zero-Breach-Toolkit-main.

### Mac

**Set up (only the first time)**

1. Go to [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/), click **Download Python**,
   open the downloaded file and follow the installer. When it finishes, open **Finder →
   Applications → Python 3** and double-click **Install Certificates.command** (without it,
   updating the indicator lists fails).
2. On this page, click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. It appears in your
   **Downloads** folder as **Zero-Breach-Toolkit-main** (if it is still a .zip file,
   double-click it).
3. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access**, click **+**, choose
   **Applications → Utilities → Terminal**, and turn it on. Without this, macOS hides
   Safari's records from the check.

**Run the check**

4. Close your web browsers and chat apps.
5. Open **Terminal** (press Cmd+Space, type `Terminal`, press Enter). Copy this line, paste it
   into Terminal and press Enter:
   ```
   cd ~/Downloads/Zero-Breach-Toolkit-main && python3 -X utf8 scan/zero-breach-toolkit.py
   ```

   then type `y` and press Enter. When it finishes, press Enter.
7. Press Enter again to start **This computer - standard check**. It takes about 15 minutes.
8. To keep a copy of the result, type `3` and press Enter, then type `.` (a full stop) and

content.readme:
# leanrea

**One 8 KB skill file that does what [REA](https://github.com/morluto/rea) does: no MCP server, no 207 tools, no setup.**

REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) puts an MCP layer between your agent and tools it can already use: asar, otool, nm, `go version -m`, jadx, apktool, Ghidra, tshark, binwalk, sqlite3. leanrea drops that layer. It tells the agent which command is fastest for each kind of target, gives it ready-to-paste recon commands, and lists the traps that REA's code handles for you. The agent then runs the real tools itself.

|  | REA 6.5.0 | leanrea |
|---|---|---|
| What gets installed | 25 MB npm package + MCP server | one `SKILL.md` |
| Instructions | 23.5 KB skill + 48.8 KB references | 8 KB |
| Tools added to the agent | 207 (3.35 MB of definitions) | 0 (uses Bash) |
| Context for "Reply OK", all tools loaded | 400.7k tokens, $1.60 | 34.5k tokens, $0.09 |

## Benchmark

Claude Code headless (`claude -p`), Sonnet 5.5, macOS arm64. 4 reverse-engineering tasks × 3 reps × 3 arms, with the arms run side by side. Answers are graded against hand-made keys.

| arm | total wall time | cost | turns | tokens | score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **leanrea** | **388 s** | **$2.17** | **55** | **2.40 M** | 74/75 |
| no skill | 479 s | $2.21 | 81 | 3.11 M | 67/75 (one refusal) |
| REA (MCP + its skill) | 627 s | $3.36 | 124 | 5.93 M | 75/75 |

Against REA, leanrea had **38% less wall time, 35% lower cost, 56% fewer turns and 60% fewer tokens, at the same accuracy**. Its one partial miss named an older IPC channel instead of the v2 one (both channels exist).

The tasks:
- **electron**: trace a feature through a real Electron app's app.asar (native function → main-process class → IPC channels).
- **native**: inventory the exports, a TCC permission check and the single-instance lock of that app's native addon (`.node`).
- **go**: toolchain and dependency versions of a stripped `gh` binary.
- **deep**: from disassembly alone, the exact socket path format, wire protocol and peer authentication of that lock.

The same operation run through REA's CLI vs the raw command:

| operation | REA | raw |
|---|---|---|
| Go build info | 0.56 s | `go version -m`: 0.06 s |
| Mach-O overview | 3.32 s | otool + dyld_info + nm: 0.04 s |
| Electron app analysis (real desktop app) | fails on asar integrity until you pass a flag, then **47.9 s and 140 MB of JSON** | asar extract + `rg -uu`: 4.8 s, 24 KB |

Full tables, the context-overhead runs and caveats: [bench/BENCHMARK.md](bench/BENCHMARK.md). Raw per-run metrics: [bench/results/final.jsonl](bench/results/final.jsonl).

**Caveats:**
- Only 3 reps per cell, one model, one machine.
- REA was tested in its best case: Claude Code's deferred tool search loads MCP tools on demand. Agents that load every tool pay the 400k-token row.
- Ghidra, Hopper and jadx weren't installed, so the native tasks ran on Xcode tools for both arms.
- The plain model is already good at this. leanrea's gain over no skill (about 19% faster, 32% fewer turns) is smaller than its gain over REA.

## Install

```sh
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea
```

This uses the [skills CLI](https://skills.sh). It finds the `leanrea` skill and asks which agents to install it for: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and the others it supports.

Common variants:
```sh
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -g                    # install for your user, in every project
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -a claude-code -y     # Claude Code only, no prompts
npx skills add aicodeking/leanrea -g -a '*' -y          # every supported agent, user level
npx skills update leanrea                               # pull the latest version later
```

Manual install, if you prefer:
```sh
git clone https://github.com/aicodeking/leanrea
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -R leanrea/leanrea ~/.claude/skills/
```
If an agent has no skills support, paste `leanrea/SKILL.md` into its rules or system prompt; it is plain text.

Use it:
```
/leanrea How does the search feature in Foo.app work? Show the evidence.
```

## What's in the skill

- **Rules:**
  - Work on a copy.
  - Route by `file` and magic bytes first.
  - Slice minified files instead of reading them.
  - Batch probes into one shell call.
  - Search extracted trees with `rg -uu`, because bundlers hide code in dot-folders like `.webpack/`.
  - Mark each claim as seen, inferred or unknown.
- **Router:** the fastest command for each target type:
  - Electron/asar (IPC, preload, `contextBridge`, fuses)
  - minified web bundles and source maps
  - Hermes/bytenode
  - Mach-O (exports, imports, entitlements, ObjC/Swift)
  - native disassembly, ELF/PE
  - Go buildinfo, Rust cargo-auditable, .NET, Android APKs, the Flutter snapshot hash
  - WASM, SQLite, plists, pcap/HAR, firmware
  - websites and runtime tracing
- **First moves:** one paste-and-run command each for native binaries and Electron apps. Each gets the whole inventory in a single tool call.
- **Speed patterns:** start f

content.readme:
# earshot

**Ears for coding agents.**

<!-- launch video -->
[**Watch the 22 s launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.1.0) - every sound in it was made
in code by `earshot forge`; no recordings, no music track.

![Frames from the launch film](docs/media/launch_frames.png)

AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.

earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.

With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.

**New in 0.4: the sound of a music-led launch film.** 51 new sounds made in code for the soft, short, mid-register
style those films use: rounded UI pops, wood and plastic knocks, short cut hits and sub hits with a kick, gated
glockenspiel / celesta / marimba notes and chime runs, water drops, camera shutters, reverse cymbals, a thump-whoosh,
short dark risers, bright swishes, burst glitches and mid dings (the bank now holds 252). A new `launch` kit preset
mixes every effect against the music bed instead of at a fixed level, says where each one sits against the cut (taps
lead it, whoosh peaks land after it) and how close a run may go. And `earshot fit` was re-made against professional
sound effects and measured on held-out clips ([below](#earshot-fit-audio-to-code)).

**New in 0.3: sound for code-made films.** A bank of sound effects stored as code that render by id in seconds,
with no models and no network: `earshot sfx` aims a whoosh, hit, click or note at a moment in the picture, and
`earshot kit` renders a whole film's effects with measured sync points ([below](#sound-for-films-bank-sfx-kits)).

```
$ earshot describe enter.ogg
  0.56 s short transient (attack 3 ms, decays in 190 ms). Sounds most like: a single mechanical keyboard key press
  (z +5.4), a soft key release click (z +3.6) ... [clear reading]. peak -0.1 dBFS, brightness 1.5 kHz ...

$ earshot match key.ogg "a deep thocky mechanical keyboard press" --alts "a clicky blue switch keyboard" "a mouse click"
  -> strong (z +3.7; would rank #2 among 322 vocabulary descriptions) ...

$ earshot find keys.ogg "a single mechanical key press" --top 4
  0:03.94-0:04.19 (0.24 s stroke, z +4.1 strong); 0:10.60-0:10.86 ...

$ earshot critique film.mp4
  VERDICT: close - 21 of 23 scored metrics in range ... FIX FIRST: 1. [major] nothing reaches body level until 0:01.01 ...
```

## What it does

| command | what an agent gets |
|---|---|
| `describe FILE` | what it sounds like: calibrated tags (z) with the closest alternative readings, AudioSet labels, measurements |
| `match FILE QUERY [--alts ...]` | how well a description fits: cosine, z among the vocabulary, a verdict (strong / plausible / weak / no match) with held-out evidence |
| `rank QUERY PATHS...` | many candidate files sorted by a description (pick the best download) |
| `find FILE QUERY` | the best moments inside a long recording, as sample trims (start / end seconds) |
| `compare FILE --refs DIR` / `ab A B` | nearest reference recordings and typicality; A/B two sounds or two trims, the differences in words |
| `realness FILE...` | real recording / pro-produced vs code-synthesized, with evidence and per-window scores |
| `timeline FILE [--video V] [--cues C]` | the listening transcript: events (time, level, tag), sections, loudness, beat grid, sync of sound to picture cuts and cue frames |
| `sheet FILE -o out.png` | an annotated PNG (video frames, sections, labelled events, spectrogram, waveform, loudness, sync markers) for agents that read images |
| `critique FILE [--video V]` | a launch-video scorecard against a profile of 7 professional launch films, with timestamped fixes |
| `profile REFS... -o p.json` | build your own reference profile from films you admire |
| `measure FILE` | objective measurements only (no models): LUFS, true peak, LRA, envelope, spectrum, tempo / key |
| `forge RECIPE --refset CAT` | make a sound in code and improve it by listening (see below) |
| `fit FILE -o recipe.py` | translate a recording into a forge recipe module that re-renders it, with knobs and morphs (see below) |
| `sfx render ID -o x.wav` | a sound from the shipped bank of 252, aimed at the picture (`--dur`, `--apex`, `--pitch`) and audited; `sfx list`, `sfx check` (no models) |
| `kit init / render / check` | a film's sound kit: on

# TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents

Aaron J. Li1, Weijia Xu2, Chandan Singh2, Zixiao Chen3, Jeevana Priya Inala2, Charlotte Siska3,
Acar Tamersoy3, Bin Yu1, Ion Stoica1, Michel Galley2, Jianfeng Gao2

1UC Berkeley   2Microsoft Research   3Microsoft Security

Our measurement on SWE-Bench tasks: 18.4–30.9% lower mean cost across five agent–model combinations, cheaper in all 30 repository × combination cells, and Pass@1 up in 4 of 5. Results

TokenEconomizer makes coding agents cheaper to run in the repositories you work in often, without changing the agent itself. It learns from the sessions an agent has already run in a repository, and uses that experience to cut waste in the sessions that follow. It has three mechanisms: - **Micro-skills: remember how the repository works.** Sessions keep rediscovering the same facts: a build step that must run first, the spelling of a command that works here (`python -m pytest` where `pytest` is missing, `npx tsc` where `tsc` is), an environment variable a command needs, where generated files live. Micro-skills learns such facts, in any language, from two sources: failures that repeat across sessions, and a model that reviews the recent sessions every *k* sessions (*k* = 3) and proposes facts. A fact is stated at the start of each session once three sessions have confirmed it, and dropped when later sessions contradict it. - **Tool pruning: stop loading tools that go unused.** Every loaded tool's definition is sent with every request. A tool that goes unused over *p* prompts spread across at least *m* sessions, or over *s* sessions of any length (*p* = 10, *m* = 2, *s* = 5), is left out of the next sessions through the agent's own settings. One command brings it back. - **Failure-loop intervention (the loop guard): step in when a turn is stuck.** When a turn (the agent's work on one prompt) keeps hitting the same failures, a judge model checks whether it is stuck. If the judge is at least *c* sure (*c* = 0.7), the agent gets a redirect (a short note, added to its context, to try another approach), at most *r* times per turn (*r* = 1). If the turn is still stuck after that, TokenEconomizer tells you how to stop it; it never stops a turn itself. # tstack

The agent skills I use every day, cleaned up so anyone can use them. They work
in Claude Code and Codex. Some use [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)
features when they are available and fall back to native tools when they are
not.

## Skills

| Skill | Say | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `full-send` | "full send" | Takes a change to a merged PR with nobody watching: proves it, reviews it, files it, babysits it, merges it. |
| `full-stop` | "full stop" | Same as `full-send`, but stops when the PR is ready for you to merge. |
| `council` | "council" | Gets review from three models from different providers, and loops until they agree. |
| `sol-loop` | "sol loop" | Reviews a change with GPT Sol in a loop until both agents agree. |
| `file-pr` | "file a PR" | Files a short PR that leads with the problem, not an inventory of changes. |
| `takeover` | "take over" | Finishes someone else's PR, branch, or agent thread, and keeps their credit. |
| `babysit-pr` | "babysit" | Watches a PR through CI and review bots, and fixes the real findings. |
| `modernize` | "modernize" | Rebases an old PR and decides if it should still exist. |
| `leaving-pr-comments` | (automatic) | Formats comments that an agent posts on your behalf. |

Some skills call others. Install the ones they need too:

- `full-send` uses `sol-loop`, `file-pr`, and `babysit-pr`.
- `full-stop` uses `full-send`.
- `takeover` uses `modernize`, `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `leaving-pr-comments`.
- `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `modernize` use `leaving-pr-comments`.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/   # Claude Code
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.codex/skills/    # Codex
```

## Requirements

- An authenticated [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`).
- `python3` for `babysit-pr`'s `pr-wait` script.
- `council` and `sol-loop` need subagents on other providers' models. T3 Code
  does this with `delegate_task`. Otherwise you need a harness that can run
  those models.

## Make them yours

These are starting points. Edit them. Put personal settings, like which models
sit on your council, in your `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, so you can update the
skills without losing them.
